method: real reeflog binary plants 3 enriched rows (live, seal-reverted, channel-only-retracted with seal still finalized); the repository harvest tool reads both channels with its zero-RPC guard; prefix = the same tool with the reorg-channel read removed
zeroRpcGuard: the tool imports tools/lib/network-guard.mjs first and exits 1 on any attempt (pinned by test/harvest-reeflog.test.mjs)

faces.claim: a signature only the retraction channel knows about must not be pinned (prefix/fixed = leak present)
no payload may be derived from a row whose seal looked live but the channel retracted
failure = the document does not name the channel-only retraction
faces.detail: prefix rowsReverted=1 lateNamed=false; fixed rowsReverted=2 lateNamed=true

faces.claim: failure = the fix dropped a live event too — the finalized row with no reorg record stays a payload source
failure = the seal-retracted row leaks (the seal gate must not be weakened by the channel work)
failure = a row the chain forgot is counted as debt hydrate could ever close

prefix.method: reeflog tail --cursor <fresh> over the local journal (envelope instructions, byte-verbatim) + reeflog reorg tail --cursor <fresh> (retraction channel)

fixed.method: reeflog tail --cursor <fresh> over the local journal (envelope instructions, byte-verbatim) + reeflog reorg tail --cursor <fresh> (retraction channel)

limits: the probe is synthetic: a planted journal, not a fork observed on mainnet
this artifact measures the CHANNEL half of the reader contract; the row SEAL half is measured in research/harvest-retraction-2026-11-16.json
one channel-only retraction; retractions for rows outside this read are covered by G1 in test/harvest-reeflog-reorg-channel.test.mjs
